name: Car Buying Checklist
description: A checklist for buying a car from start to finish.

items.text: Decide a maximum total budget and a comfortable monthly payment.
Include insurance, fuel or charging, maintenance and taxes.
items.note: The purchase price is only part of the total cost of ownership.

items.text: Determine your down payment or trade-in value.
Check your credit score before seeking financing.
Avoid stretching the budget to a longer loan term.
Leave room for registration, fees and an emergency fund.
List your needs — size, seats, cargo, fuel type and use case.
Compare models on reliability, safety ratings and reviews.
Research typical pricing for the models you want.
Check fuel economy or range and expected running costs.
Look into insurance costs for shortlisted models.
Read about common problems and recalls for each model.
Get pre-approved by a bank or credit union for a benchmark rate.
items.note: Pre-approval gives you leverage to compare against dealer financing.

items.text: Compare the APR, loan length and total interest of each offer.
Avoid focusing only on the monthly payment.
Confirm there is no prepayment penalty.
Decide on a cash, loan or lease approach.
Have your trade-in valued independently before negotiating.
Inspect the car's condition in daylight before driving.
Test drive on varied roads, including highway speeds.
Check comfort, visibility, controls and tech.
Listen for noises and feel for vibration or pulling.
Verify the features and trim match what is advertised.
Test the parking, mirrors and driver-assistance systems.
Negotiate the out-the-door price, not the monthly payment.
Get quotes from multiple sellers to compare.
Negotiate the trade-in separately from the purchase price.
Question and decline unwanted add-ons and dealer fees.
items.note: Some dealer add-ons carry high margins and little value — ask about each.

items.text: Be prepared to walk away if the terms are not right.
Get every agreed figure in writing before proceeding.
Review the contract line by line, including all fees.
Confirm the price, financing and any included items match the deal.
Verify the VIN, mileage and vehicle details on the paperwork.
Arrange insurance to be active before you drive away.
Complete the title transfer and registration.
Collect all keys, manuals, receipts and a copy of every document.

faq.q: What is a car buying checklist?
faq.a: It's a step-by-step guide for buyers covering budget, research, financing, the test drive, negotiation and paperwork, so you work through buying a car methodically and avoid overpaying or signing terms you'll regret.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a car?
faq.a: Factor in the total cost of ownership, not just the price — financing, insurance, fuel or charging, maintenance, taxes and registration. Set a firm budget before shopping and avoid stretching it under sales pressure.

faq.q: Should I get financing before going to the dealer?
faq.a: Getting pre-approved from a bank or credit union gives you a benchmark rate and negotiating power. Compare it against dealer financing and read all terms, including the rate, length and any fees, before signing.

faq.q: What should I do before signing the paperwork?
faq.a: Confirm the final price, all fees and the financing terms in writing, check that add-ons are ones you actually want, and never sign anything you don't understand. For a used car, get a professional inspection first.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the car buying checklist to keep with you while shopping, or download the PDF to track options and offers on your phone.
